title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' Grothendieck studies the profinite modular situation. ρ and σ are the finite-order 'inertia' data of orders 2 and 3, and L_ρ, L_σ, L_0 are the corresponding inertia subgroups. 𝔊 is the profinite (free) fundamental group and 𝔊^+ is the index-≤2 subgroup on which the relevant character is trivial. G_{ρ,σ} is an extension 1→𝔊^+→G_{ρ,σ}→γ_{ρ,σ}→1, where γ_{ρ,σ} is a quotient carrying a cyclotomic character χ_γ:γ→Ẑ^*. N_ρ^*, N_σ^* are 'augmented normalizers' of L_ρ, L_σ. They map onto γ_{ρ,σ} by δ_ρ, δ_σ with kernels SN_ρ ≅ Norm_𝔊(L_ρ) and SN_σ ≅ Norm_𝔊(L_σ). The previous page records these, together with the injectivity of N_ρ^*, N_σ^* into G_{ρ,σ}.

What this page does.
(i) It records the kernels SN_ρ = Ker(N_ρ→γ) ≅ Norm_𝔊(L_ρ) and SN_σ = Norm_𝔊(L_σ). It then crosses out an analogous line for an object B_{ρ,σ}, whose kernel would be ≅ L_0 ⊂ Cent_𝔊(L_0) ∩ Norm_𝔊(L_0). The object B is renamed 𝐙_{ρ,σ}: an extension of γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0, so that S𝐙_{ρ,σ} = Ker(𝐙→γ) ≅ L_0. A marginal, crossed-out remark says that it would follow from (15) that in the cases considered Norm_𝔊(L_0) = Cent_𝔊(L_0), 'et itou pour L_ρ, L_σ'.
(ii) Definitions (50)–(51): iterated fibre products over γ = γ_{ρ,σ}.
- S_0M = 𝐙 ×_γ N_ρ^* ×_γ N_σ^* ×_γ G_{ρ,σ} and M = N_ρ^* ×_γ N_σ^* ×_γ G_{ρ,σ}.
- S_0Γ = 𝐙 ×_γ N_ρ^* ×_γ N_σ^* and Γ = N_ρ^* ×_γ N_σ^*.
The last factor in M is G_{ρ,σ}, not C; the next page uses τ'_G ∈ G_{ρ,σ}.
(iii) Diagram (52): forgetting the G-factor gives 1→𝔊^+→M→Γ→1 and 1→𝔊^+→S_0M→S_0Γ→1. Forgetting the 𝐙-factor gives vertical surjections with kernel L_0. The diagram is the 3×3 diagram of these two compatible extensions.
(iv) Sequences (53)–(56): the kernel of a fibre product of groups over γ, mapping to γ, is the product of the individual kernels. This gives 1 → L_0×SN_ρ×SN_σ×𝔊^+ → S_0M → γ → 1, and likewise for M, S_0Γ and Γ.

Purpose. The next page notes that S_0M ≅ M ×_γ 𝐙, i.e. the L_0-extensions are pulled back from the basic extension 𝐙 of γ by L_0. It then embeds Ẑ^+ diagonally into M via the 'avatars' τ'_M = (τ'_ρ, τ'_σ, τ'_G) of an element τ'. The aim is a single group in which an element of GT-type and its local avatars at the three cusps/inertia points live simultaneously and compatibly over the common quotient γ. This is a set-up for writing the loop equation (the 2- and 3-cycle relations) as a condition inside such a fibre product.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page. The exactness claims are formal consequences of all factors surjecting onto γ_{ρ,σ}, which the construction requires implicitly.
The diagram labels the kernel of S_0M→M as L_0; this uses S𝐙_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0, which is asserted rather than proved here.
The machine transcription's 'C_{ρ,σ}' should be G_{ρ,σ}.

ideas.what: Kernels of the augmented normalizers N_ρ^*, N_σ^* → γ_{ρ,σ} identified with normalizers in 𝔊 of the inertia subgroups L_ρ, L_σ
ideas.modern_name: normalizers of inertia/finite subgroups in profinite (orbifold) fundamental groups; decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for the modular orbifold)

ideas.what: Assembling local normalizer data and the global extension G_{ρ,σ} as an iterated fibre product over a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ}, with diagonally embedded 'avatars' of an automorphism
ideas.modern_name: fibre products of group extensions; a local–global compatibility group akin to the setting of the defining relations of GT̂
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; GT̂ setting due to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara

deep.surprise_reason: The page is pure bookkeeping: definitions of fibre-product groups and formally exact sequences in the set-up of the loop equation. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's larger unpublished GT-type programme, not in itself.
transcription_corrections: In (50)/(51), M_{ρ,σ} and S_0M_{ρ,σ} have last factor G_{ρ,σ}, not C_{ρ,σ}.
The bold letter 'Z_{ρ,σ}' is overwritten on a 'B'; it is the renamed B_{ρ,σ}, an extension of γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0.
The fraktur letter is 𝔊 (and 𝔊^+), not 𝔖, consistent with the previous page.
Marginal crossed-out note reads roughly: 'Il suivrait que (15) dans les cas que … Norm_𝔊(L_0) [= Cent_𝔊(L_0)] … et itou pour L_ρ, L_σ'.
The first line is likely S N_ρ (rendered SZ_ρ in the transcription), parallel to SN_σ; the final '≅ Norm_𝔊(L_ρ)' is struck through.
